_comment: The PERMISSION vocabulary — what an actor is allowed to do, independent of any process. Split out of `actors[].capabilities` on 2026-09-18 (bean ind9), which had been carrying three different things: environment probes, permissions, and skills. Schema: schemas/role-graph.ts. WHY THESE ARE ACTOR PROPERTIES AND NOT ROLE PROPERTIES, which was tested rather than assumed: a permission CROSS-CUTS roles. `content-authoring` is held by actors taking on five different roles (author, authoring-agent, evidence-agent, ingestion-agent, onboarding-agent); `qa-reporting` by three (build-pipeline, ig-publisher-service, qc-reviewer); and `admin` holds `admin-settings` in every one of the five lanes it acts in. Moving them onto Role produced 36 conflicts where a permission was held by some but not all actors sharing a role. A skill answers WHAT THE PERFORMER NEEDS TO KNOW and belongs to the lane; a permission answers WHAT THIS PARTICIPANT MAY DO and travels with the participant.
name: folio-assistant

permissions.title: Author content
permissions.description: May create and modify content blocks. Held by every actor that writes, human or agentic.

permissions.title: Leave review comments
permissions.description: May record findings on a change. Deliberately distinct from accepting one — see `approval-authority`.

permissions.title: Approve and sign off
permissions.description: May formally accept a change and gate a phase transition. The separation from `review-comments` is the point: reviewing is advice, approving is a decision.

permissions.title: Adjudicate a disagreement
permissions.description: May settle a criterion whose reviewer entries disagree, and write the entry that leads it — with a reason. Neither `review-comments` (record a finding) nor `approval-authority` (accept a change): the subject here is two findings that contradict each other, and the holder chooses between them without the change itself being accepted or rejected. Cross-cuts roles like every permission, and measurably so — adjudication happens in four lanes bound to `narrative-reviewer`, `translation-adjudicator`, `reviewer` and `user`. See skills/folio-core/adjudication.md.

permissions.title: First-pass review
permissions.description: May perform the triage review that decides whether a change reaches an SME at all.

permissions.title: Coordinate SMEs
permissions.description: May route work to subject-matter experts and hold them to a schedule.

permissions.title: Validate clinically
permissions.description: May rule on whether content is clinically accurate and complete. Not a review of the artefact — a judgement about the subject matter.

permissions.title: Translate content
permissions.description: May produce target-language text for a source block.

permissions.title: Emit QA reports
permissions.description: May produce the QA findings a gate reads. Cross-cutting by design: a human QC reviewer and a build pipeline both hold it.

permissions.title: Govern the programme
permissions.description: May set scope, form the team, allocate resources and hold the timeline.

permissions.title: Authorise a release
permissions.description: May authorise publication. One of the steps `folio:policy relaxable="false"` marks non-negotiable; no workflow policy may relax it.

permissions.title: Manage a release
permissions.description: May configure, build, version and deploy a release once it has been authorised. Distinct from authorising it.

permissions.title: Change instance settings
permissions.description: May change the instance's own configuration.

permissions.title: Manage role assignments
permissions.description: May change which actors exist and which roles they may take on — the assignment table itself.
